A.lost: The case is settled at the funder's withdrawal floor rather than the plaintiff's, once the defendant learns who can close the chest and sits below that line.

B.lost: The strike collapses when the counted weeks run out, and the wages spent waiting buy none of the concessions the number was meant to force.

C.lost: The deals given up on the counterparties' testing schedule to keep the record, and the present deal's terms when the record is read as stale.

D.lost: The price the round was going to clear at, the moment the lead learns the only alternative is the insiders and that no outsider came.

E.lost: The sale unwound or the ringer's accidental win let off, and the seller's standing in the venue once a lot that never closed reappears and names the conspiracy.

F.lost: The round's terms when the investor calls a cut the company never made, or the team and product that go with the cut if it is made to prove the state.

G.lost: The second source, which stops quoting after learning it was the stalking horse, leaving the incumbent's price unopposed until another suitor is fed.

H.lost: The deal that dies at the brink for a holder with a real floor, or every later concession priced off the fold for a holder whose calm broke in the last hour.

I.lost: The round from the incumbent and the founder's word in a market small enough that one checked and false name is the story that follows the next raise.

J.lost: A quarterly slice of the company's information handed to a party that is keeping the founder warm as its own option, never itemized on any ledger.

K.lost: The gap between the court-approved floor and the price a contested auction would have found, plus the fee paid to a horse chosen because it would win.

L.lost: The outside offer that actually expires on its date, or, if the party is seen still seated after it, every deadline this party ever names again.

M.lost: The private table, ended the moment the letter goes, and the audience's one-shot attention spent on this table rather than any later one.

N.lost: The company liquidated or the settlement handed to the regulator to make the threat believable, or the whole concession when a counterparty finds nothing burned in the record and calls it.

O.lost: The terms the counterparty's prior was holding up, gone the day the model of the holder's kind updates, with nothing built to replace them and no claim that would not invite the check.

P.lost: The town's disputes returned to the lord's court when the crown stops needing the town or stops wanting the charter to be real, discovered on the day the door is tried.

Q.lost: The price the certificate was holding down, and, if the second line has been untooled, the switch the certificate said could be made.

R.lost: The constraint's standing with this counterparty once the money is found, and with it every future refusal this party makes on an absent principal's behalf.
